architecture_decisions: 5.1 Persistence The model refactor must produce one SQLAlchemy metadata graph. Focused modules may define domain groups, but imports through the historical `parallax_api.models` surface remain compatible until callers are deliberately migrated.

AC-01: validate protected requirement — P2-V0.24.0 is implemented inside the existing FastAPI/SQLAlchemy API and Expo/React/Skia client. No greenfield Next.js replacement or competing application shell is introduced.

AC-02: validate protected requirement — Focused model modules share one canonical SQLAlchemy metadata graph, historical `parallax_api.models` imports remain compatible, and clean SQLite/PostgreSQL schema checks pass for the supported tables, constraints and indexes.

AC-03: validate protected requirement — Clean initialization creates required schema, while an existing database is never silently dropped, truncated or rebuilt. Any historical data cutover is explicit, separately validated and not inferred from code generation.

AC-04: validate protected requirement — Engineering Run transitions, run events and worker execution persistence preserve owner scope, expected revision, atomicity, monotonic sequence, exact lease ownership, replay safety and rollback/recovery semantics while reducing avoidable database round trips.

AC-05: validate protected requirement — A controlled benchmark against the exact P2-V0.23.50 baseline demonstrates at least 40% improvement for the defined Engineering Run transition/event persistence path with the same correctness assertions.

AC-06: validate protected requirement — Focused tests prove exact accepted-lineage checks, active-lease single-flight, expired-lease recovery, stale revision rejection and rollback/retry behavior are unchanged or stricter.

AC-07: validate protected requirement — Any new/refined cache uses deterministic keys plus bounded invalidation/TTL behavior and cannot bypass authentication, revision, lease, lineage, protected evidence, lifecycle or provider checks.

AC-08: validate protected requirement — Autonomy coordination, implementation/candidate execution and durable mutation responsibilities are separated enough that candidate/execution helpers cannot mutate unrelated Engineering Run lifecycle state or provider authority implicitly.

AC-09: validate protected requirement — DSPy programs/compiler code may be optimized, but protected evaluator implementations, thresholds, promotion rules and promotion-suite expected contracts are neither optimizer inputs nor optimizer-controlled outputs. Protected promotion gates remain deterministic.

AC-10: validate protected requirement — A provider-independent development/test intelligence path produces deterministic contract-valid outputs for covered compiler/program regression cases and records that it is an offline development path rather than provider-backed production intelligence.

AC-11: validate protected requirement — Source delivery consumes only exact verified accepted lineage under the canonical Project delivery mode. Delivery failure does not rewrite protected lifecycle success, and `vercel-preview` grants no merge, default-branch or production-promotion authority.

AC-12: validate protected requirement — The stream requires the same owner-scoped authentication as canonical reads, validates run ownership and cursor, replays durable events after the cursor in monotonic order, follows new durable events, and bounds replay/heartbeat behavior.

AC-13: validate protected requirement — Client reconnect preserves only an observation cursor, resumes without duplicate-authority assumptions, and reconciles through canonical read APIs after gaps/errors. Poll/read fallback remains safe when streaming is unavailable.

AC-14: validate protected requirement — The existing Warm Editorial Observatory visual language, conversation-primary hierarchy, desktop/mobile reachability, nested technical scrolling, keyboard operation, readable text, reduced motion and screen-reader state semantics pass client/browser validation.

AC-15: validate protected requirement — The candidate passes changed-spec validation, authentic DSPy compiled-plan validation, focused API/client tests, cross-database schema checks, performance gate, full relevant API/client/protected release gates and records generated, validated, deployed and deployment-verified states distinctly.

critique: The current architecture and model modularization preserve one schema contract, historical `parallax_api.models` imports remain compatible, and clean SQLite and PostgreSQL databases. The database initialization is non-destructive, and clean initialization creates required schema. The repository hot paths retain protected semantics, and the transition latency improves by at least 40 percent. The same-lineage, lease and rollback regressions remain green. The cache cannot become authority, and the execution responsibilities are narrower, and the DSPy optimization stays outside protected evaluation, offline intelligence is deterministic, and the delivery remains isolated and Preview-bounded. The streaming reconnect reconciles with canonical state, and the workspace behavior and accessibility do not regress. The release evidence stays truthful.
